_comment: THE RACE STORY. How a driver's afternoon has actually gone.
Built from `story.Arc`, which is measured and never inferred. A category
is only offered when `Arc.headline()` returns it, so no line here can be
said about a driver it is untrue of.
SLOTS:
{drv}   the driver
{grid}  where he started      'twelfth'
{pos}   where he is now       'fourth'
{n}     the number of places involved, as a phrase: 'nine places'
{worst} the lowest he fell to 'nineteenth'
{best}  the highest he reached
{offs}  'twice' / 'three times'
THESE LINES ARE DELIBERATELY LONGER THAN THE REST OF THE PRODUCT.
The user's complaint was exact: 'they just give one statement and then
there is no conversation, it is like Max is a 9 time race winner, full
stop'. So a story line is two clauses: WHAT happened, and then what it
MEANS or costs. That second half is what makes it sound like somebody
watching rather than a scoreboard being read out.
The ANALYST answers are longer still — he is being asked a question and a
one-line answer to a direct question is the thing that reads as a script.
His cap is 32 words and these use it.
ERA-NEUTRAL BY CONSTRUCTION. Nothing here names a piece of equipment, a
regulation or a decade, so every line is legal in 1966 and in 2025 and
Brett can deliver all of it. That is deliberate: a race story is the one
thing that has never changed about this sport.
THE WRAP. Four lines was not a wrap: podium, championship lead, one Chuck
verdict, goodbye. Nothing about how the top drivers actually drove, no
separate opinion from Chuck, and 'the championship lead belongs to X' was
the entire championship implication.
`wrap_ask` -> a `story_*` answer reuses the mid-race machinery, so the man
who was described as recovering on lap thirty is described the same way at
the flag. Written once, told consistently.
`wrap_impressed` is CHUCK'S OWN PICK and deliberately not the winner. The
booth already has a dozen ways to praise whoever won; the thing a viewer
cannot get anywhere else is which OTHER drive was worth watching.

story_ask.t: What do you make of {drv}'s race so far, Chuck?
Give me a read on {drv}, Chuck.
Chuck — {drv}. How is that one going?
Talk to me about {drv}'s race, Chuck.
Where does {drv} stand in all this, Chuck?
How would you sum up {drv}'s day so far?
Chuck, has {drv} had the race he wanted?

story_recovery.t: He was as low as {worst}, and he is {pos} now. {n} taken back by driving rather than luck — you can see it in how he sets the car up.
The recovery of the race. Down to {worst}, back to {pos}, and not one wild move in it — he has simply been quicker than the car in front, over and over.
{drv} lost everything early and has spent the rest of the afternoon getting it back. {worst} to {pos}. That takes patience most drivers do not have.
From {worst} to {pos}. What I like about it is that he never forced it — he waited, he picked them off, and he has not put a wheel wrong since.
He has climbed {n} from his lowest point, and every one of those was earned on track. That is a proper drive, whatever the result says at the end.

story_charge.t: He started {grid} and he is {pos}. {n} gained, and none of it handed to him — he has passed every single one of those cars on the road.
{n} up on where he started, and he has done it without a moment of drama. That is the hardest way to make progress and the one that lasts.
From {grid} on the grid to {pos}. He got a start, he kept his head, and he has been picking cars off ever since.
This is what a good afternoon looks like — {grid} to {pos}, steadily, without ever looking like he was going to throw it away.
He has made {n} and he is not finished. Whatever happens from here, that drive is the reason we will still be talking about this race.

story_slide.t: He has gone the wrong way. As high as {best}, down to {pos} — and that looks like a car that has stopped working underneath him, not a driver making mistakes.
{drv} is going backwards, and quickly. {best} to {pos}. Something has changed with that car, because the driving has not.
This is a race unravelling. He held {best} comfortably and he has lost {n} since, which usually means tyres and occasionally means something worse.
He is defending now, and he has been defending for a while. {best} down to {pos} — that is a man hanging on rather than racing.

story_undone.t: He has undone his own race. {best} down to {pos} — and it was not the car. Off {offs}, and you cannot do that and expect a result.
Self-inflicted, this one. He was running {best}, he has been off {offs}, and each one cost him places he then had to fight back for.
{drv} has thrown this away himself. The pace was there all afternoon, but you cannot visit the scenery {offs} and finish where you deserve.
There is a quick driver in that car getting in his own way. {best} to {pos}, off {offs} — and none of it was necessary.

story_scrappy.t: A scruffy afternoon. Off {offs} now, and each one costs him a couple of seconds he then spends two laps getting back.
He is on the edge of it and he has been over the edge {offs}. There is real pace there, but it is coming with a lot of drama attached.
{drv} is driving right at the limit and occasionally past it — off {offs} today. Exciting to watch, expensive to do.
He keeps finding the run-off. {offs} now. At some point that stops being bad luck and starts being a driver asking too much of the car.

story_led.t: He has led this from the front and made it look ordinary, which it is not. Nobody has been close enough to make him think about it.
This is control rather than dominance. He has managed the gap, managed the tyres, and never once given the man behind a reason to believe.
{drv} has been in front the whole way and the hardest part of that is the concentration. One mistake in an hour and the race is somebody else's.
Leading a race is not the same as being quickest in it. He has spent the afternoon doing exactly enough, which is its own skill.

story_dropping.t: {drv} has lost {n} from his grid slot and he does not look like he has an answer for it. That is a long afternoon from here.
He qualified {grid} and he is {pos}. Whatever they found on Saturday, they have not got it today.
This is going the wrong way for {drv}. {n} lost, and the cars going past him are not making a meal of it, which tells you it is pace.
He is being picked off, and there is nothing more demoralising in this sport than watching a mirror fill up when you already know you cannot respond.

story_progress.t: Quietly good. {grid} to {pos}, no mistakes — and at the end of a race that is usually what a result looks like.
He has made {n} without anybody noticing, which is exactly how you want to make them. No drama, no damage, just steady progress.
{drv} is up on where he started and he has been sensible about it. That is a driver racing the whole distance rather than the first ten laps.
Modest, but it is going the right way. {grid} to {pos}, and there is more in it if the car in front makes a mistake.

story_losing.t: He has slipped a couple of places and he is not looking comfortable. Not a disaster, but this is not the afternoon he came for.
{grid} to {pos}. It is only {n}, but he has been going backwards steadily rather than losing them in one moment, and that is the harder problem.
A quiet slide. Nothing has gone wrong, exactly — he is just a little slower than the people around him and it adds up over a race distance.

story_holding.t: He has held his grid slot all afternoon. That sounds like nothing and is quite hard — nobody past him, and not one mistake.
Exactly where he started, and completely clean. Some races are about maximising what you have rather than finding something extra.
{drv} has done what he needed to. {pos} on the grid, {pos} now, no mistakes and nothing thrown away.

story_out.t: His race is over, and it was going well until it was not. That is the cruel part of this — an hour of good work and nothing to show for it.
He is out, and he will be replaying that one for a while. There is nothing worse than a result taken away from you rather than lost.
That is {drv} done for the afternoon. Whatever the cause, the drive he had put in deserved better than this.

story_from_quali.t: Remember where this one came from. He found it at the end of qualifying, and a lap like that changes an entire afternoon.
He earned that grid slot late on Saturday, and you can see he is racing with the confidence of a man who knows the lap was in there.
That qualifying lap is why he is where he is. Everything he has done today has been built on it.
He put it on pole when it mattered, at the end of the session, with everybody watching. That is a different kind of pressure to this.

wrap_ask_impressed.t: Chuck, forget the winner for a moment. Who impressed you out there?
Whose drive did you enjoy most today, Chuck?
Chuck — anybody else catch your eye this afternoon?
Give me a drive of the day, Chuck. Not the winner.
Who else is worth talking about, Chuck?
Chuck, who else deserves a mention before we go?

wrap_impressed.t: {drv}, for me. {grid} on the grid and {pos} at the flag, and he did it without a single moment that made you wince.
I would give it to {drv}. Nobody was talking about him at the start and he has finished {pos}. That is a proper afternoon's work.
{drv}. He has taken {n} on a day when the cars around him could not, and that is usually a driver rather than a car.
For me it is {drv}. He got everything there was out of that car and then a little more, which is all you can ask.
{drv}, and it is not close. {grid} to {pos}, clean the whole way, and no help from anybody.
I liked {drv}. It was not spectacular and it was never going to lead the highlights, but it was the most complete drive out there.

champ_extends.t: That stretches the championship lead to {pts} points, with {left} still to run.
{leader} leaves here {pts} points clear, and there are only {left} left to change it.
The gap at the top is {pts} now. With {left} remaining, that is starting to look like a cushion.
{pts} points in hand and {left} to go. This championship is going one way at the moment.

champ_closes.t: The championship just got closer — {pts} points covering the top two with {left} to run.
That is {pts} points between them now. {left} left, and this is a title fight again.
{pts} points and {left} to run. Whatever anybody thought was settled about this championship, it is not.
The gap comes down to {pts}. That result changes the whole complexion of this season.

champ_next.t: {left} to go, and every one of them matters more than the last after that.
There are {left} left. On that evidence, whoever wins this championship is going to have earned it.
With {left} remaining, the pressure moves onto the man in front. It always does.
{left} to run. The interesting part is that neither of them can afford a bad afternoon now.
